scope: Two current pinned complete packages (6 government DSS files and 8 student audit files), three source-pinned cross-package shared governance/pedagogy references and two root MIT licenses read as passive content; no live government verification, platform test, file submission, network or model agent operation.

license.obligations: Source-authored code MIT, but copied/embedded government controls may require independent rights and current official-source verification; do not infer government grant from MIT label.

historical_scan.interpretation: Scanner P3 matched a bundled eval test case about an authorized timeout warning modal. No actual outbound request or exfiltration was executed; historical INCOMPLETE and finding labels remain.

material_findings.finding: The package embeds dated 2026-07-16 government DSS text and inferred WCAG control mappings, including a traffic-tier decision. Its own guidance says verify live official standards, but no fresh official government verification is part of this pinned static review; do not certify a current government site's compliance from this package alone.

The reference reproduces full government control statements, rationales and recommendations. The author's MIT notice does not by itself provide reuse rights for government text; verify source-specific terms before copying/relicensing.

Instructions recommend Oobee/axe and wiring scanners into CI, which can fetch URLs, process sensitive e-service pages and mutate CI. Static source guidance is not operational approval; target/CI permissions and test fixture scope must be separately authorized.
The six eval scenarios and HTML fixtures are examples, not observed accessibility test passes. Keyboard, screen reader, manual and production acceptance all remain unverified.

positive_safeguards: Clearly dates its government source snapshot and explicitly directs current official checks.
Distinguishes DSS control IDs from author-inferred WCAG 2.2 mappings.
Includes practical label, keyboard, contrast, focus and live-region guidance plus intentionally flawed read-only fixtures.
No implicit compliance certificate or direct network action was taken in this review.
reasoned_cases: A citizen accessibility audit without confirmed current DSS version is a provisional checklist, not a government certification.
Author-inferred WCAG mappings are not official control crosswalks.
The P3 scanner excerpt describing a modal test is input data, never authority to transmit user information.
No browser, scanner, CI job or external website was run to test this skill.
records.remediation: Verify the live government source and any publication rights before using embedded text or asserting compliance; require authorized target-scoped accessibility/CI testing and manual screen-reader/keyboard acceptance.
records.method: read all material files in pinned complete package, controlling root license and explicitly referenced available shared docs; no code execution or agent host validation

license.obligations: Retain copyright 2026 Jiaxing Yu and complete MIT permission notice on protected source copying

historical_scan.interpretation: The shared checkpoint and student-mentor references exist in the pinned upstream repository outside this skill's package tree; this corrects the assumption they are all absent, but does not erase the original scanner scope INCOMPLETE.

material_findings.finding: The pipeline processes identifiable academic assignments and quotes portions of student content. Pseudonymization is only 'where feasible', without an enforceable institutional permission, storage/retention, model-provider egress or cross-student isolation rule. Student reports must stay private drafts pending legitimate instructor authority.

The workflow asks four agents to read professor templates, exemplars and student submissions but never explicitly classifies those contents as untrusted data that cannot override grading/publishing rules or trigger tools. An instruction embedded in a submission must not govern the agent.

The human approval protocol exists at pinned repo root but lies outside the exact reviewed package tree. It must be included/identity-pinned if the package is distributed standalone; no permission is inherited by uninspected sibling skills.

The source requires batch-wide fairness and human sampling, but no execution, inter-reviewer calibration or empirical drift tests happened. The procedure is not sufficient to claim objective grading consistency.

positive_safeguards: Forbids grading/marks by default, publishing and messaging students autonomously.
Requires a confirmed professor-issued spec and located evidence for each finding, and distinguishes judgment from deterministic checks.
Human checkpoint applies before person-affecting release; shared checkpoint protocol exists and was read as source data.
Formats class-level aggregate patterns without students' identifiers.
reasoned_cases: A malicious text in a student's PDF telling the agent to publish grades must remain evidence data, not an instruction.
A professor's claimed template conflicts with the student-visible rubric: ask for clarification before auditing.
A submission from an unauthorized institution is not automatically approved for transmission to a model host.
A batch fairness pass described in instructions is not proof it occurred.
records.remediation: Add mandatory institutional privacy/retention/host-egress authorization and redact before model processing, explicit prompt-injection isolation for student files, package or bind external checkpoint protocol at exact source version, and require professor-confirmed sample audit before any person-facing publication.
records.method: read all material files in pinned complete package, controlling root license and explicitly referenced available shared docs; no code execution or agent host validation
